newsitem.title: GERMANY: Northern Europe rapeseed firms on low supplies.
newsitem.headline: Northern Europe rapeseed firms on low supplies.

text.p: Northern Europe rapeseed prices rose as poor harvests in some countries left buyers without sufficient supply while farmers hoarded large volumes, brokers said on Friday.
"Farmers sold about 30-35 percent of the new crop in pre-harvest contracts, but the rest won't be available for some time to come," one said.
"Normally, this would cause price rallies but it is being offset by weak demand for oil and good rapeseed harvests in France and Britain."
Buyers free Hamburg offered 470 marks/tonne, five marks more than last week and 30 marks more than six weeks ago.
Subsequent delivery prices should rise four marks a tonne per month until December.
Canadian canola was offered at $340 but was uncompetitive in small quantities.
One broker estimated some 100,000 tonnes had been sold from Canada's ample new crop into Europe but the anticipated heavy canola influx here would take another four to six weeks to develop.
With Scandinavian and Polish processors in short supply, brokers believed prices had some upside potential short term.
They also cited the strong dollar versus the mark and reasonable meal demand.
Sellers might be reactivated if rapeseed reached 480 marks.
Rapeseed buyers at points other than Hamburg offered five to 10 marks more for September than last week, with bids in a 455-470 marks range.
The November position on the Paris Matif futures exchange last traded two marks above last night's close at 475 marks.
Local rape meal sellers quoted Sept/October meal (34 percent protein) at 28.75-29.00 marks/100 kg, up 0.25-0.50 on last week, while Nov/Jan was up 0.25 at 28.50 marks.

In comparison, spot soymeal cost 45.50-45.75 marks (44 percent protein). Sept, Oct and Nov-Jan rape oil were each up 2.75 marks at 88.75, 89 and 91 marks respectively. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
